title: Fabrication Controlled Vocabulary
description: A controlled vocabulary of the KEYS a manifest's fabrication fields write (SEM-1 §4): the processes a part can be made by, the material classes it may be made of, the slicer parameters a requirement profile constrains, the capabilities a producer machine declares, and the size keys two mating interfaces must share. It is a SIBLING of commons-vocabulary.schema.json, not an extension of it, because the two describe different things: a commons vocabulary is a reading of what the two commons' manifests already wrote (keys observed in a corpus, an English gloss, a pointer at a lexicon term), while a fabrication vocabulary is a reference list whose entries are not observed anywhere yet and carry their own meaning — quadrilingual labels and definitions (RFC 0039), dimensional and technical facts each tied to a public citation, and cross-maps to outside identifiers (Cotiza process codes, OrcaSlicer config keys, material-card slugs, EMMO classes). A key's MADFAM concept IRI is derived, never stored: https://id.madfam.io/concept/{vocabulary}/{key}.

spec_version.description: Version of THIS vocabulary contract the document is written against.

vocabulary.description: Which vocabulary this document is. One file per vocabulary, named for it.

description.description: What this vocabulary covers and what it deliberately does not.

review.description: Whether the document's rulings (which keys exist, what each one means) have had a human pass. Per-language review of the labels and definitions lives on each entry.

key.description: The identifier exactly as a manifest writes it. Lowercase alphanumerics separated by '-', '_' or '.': each vocabulary keeps the spelling its outside world already uses (OrcaSlicer's snake_case keys, Cotiza-adjacent process codes, the dotted pitch in 'stack-30.5x30.5-m3'). Every key is a valid IRI path segment, so the derived concept IRI needs no escaping.

quadrilingualString.description: A string in all four languages of the commons (RFC 0039). Spanish is the house register and the quality bar.

reviewState.description: `generated` — written in a drafting pass (by a contributor or an agent) and not yet checked by a speaker of the language. `reviewed` — a named reviewer has read it in that language and let it stand.

reviewStatus.description: The same review block a lexicon term carries (lexicon-term.schema.json, contract 2): the overall state is the WORST facet, and `reviewed` needs a named reviewer.

externalIdentifier.description: An identifier minted outside MADFAM: an absolute IRI, or an ECLASS IRDI (identifiers only — ECLASS content is licensed and never copied).

source.description: A public citation a reader can follow: a standard, a manufacturer datasheet or product page, or a source file at a pinned revision. `supports` says which facts it backs. Dimensions are facts; datasheet prose is never copied.

status.description: `canonical` (default) — the spelling to write. `provisional` — real and usable, but a fact or a ruling on it is still open; `notes` says which.

label.description: The short name of the key in each language — what a form or a dictionary shows.

definition.description: What the key means, in each language.

term.description: A lexicon term this key is an instance of, when one exists (e.g. build-volume). Validated against the corpus.

exact_match.description: Outside identifiers of the SAME concept (SKOS exactMatch).

close_match.description: Outside identifiers of a CLOSE concept (SKOS closeMatch). May not repeat an exact_match.

sources.description: The citations behind this entry's facts. REQUIRED wherever the entry states a dimensional or technical fact; a dimension cites its source by index.

family.description: Additive (builds the part up), subtractive (cuts it out of stock in 3-D), or cutting (2-D profiles out of sheet).

iso_52900_category.description: The ISO/ASTM 52900 additive-manufacturing process category, for additive processes.

cotiza_code.description: The process code Cotiza (digifab-quoting) accepts for this process. Absent where Cotiza has no code yet — the gap is a fact worth seeing, not something to paper over with the nearest code.

cardRef.description: A material card in one of the two commons, as '<repo>/<slug>' — resolved against the bundled catalog snapshot.

kind.description: The stock form the class arrives in.

processes.description: Keys of the `processes` vocabulary this class is made with. A technical claim: the entry's sources back it. Required for every kind except `fabric` — a woven or knit class is cut and sewn, which no process key names yet, and the lane says so rather than inventing one.

emmo_class.description: The EMMO class the commons' material cards of this class record (yantra4d `semantic_ontology.emmo_class`). Copied from the cards, not asserted independently: when the cards of one class disagree, the class records none and says so in `notes`.

cards.description: The material cards that belong to this class, as '<repo>/<slug>'.

orcaslicerBinding.description: Where this key is defined in OrcaSlicer's own source, so the claim that the key is OrcaSlicer's is checkable at a revision.

option_type.description: The ConfigOption type in PrintConfig.cpp (coInt, coFloat, coFloats, coPercent, coBool, coEnum, coInts …).

preset.description: Which OrcaSlicer preset carries the key (Preset.cpp option lists), or `placeholder` for a value OrcaSlicer exposes only to custom G-code.

unit.description: The unit a requirement bound is written in. `percent` is 0–100; `count` is a whole number of layers or loops; `none` for booleans and enums.

value_type.description: The JSON type a machine-model declaration writes for this capability.

allowed_values.description: The closed set of string values (each a key in its own right), for enumerated capabilities.

value_vocabulary.description: Another fabrication vocabulary whose keys are this capability's values (e.g. `process` takes `processes` keys).

dimension.description: One dimensional or technical fact, citing the entry's `sources` by index.

geometry_type.description: The yantra4d interface geometry type (a `geometry_type` key of the `interfaces` vocabulary) an interface carrying this size key has.

dimensions.description: The size key's dimensional facts, by name. Every one cites a source.
